So what you're saying is that the people you describe as “most critics” are merely trying to “limit specific ideologies and traits through cultural pushback and policy changes,” and that violence is not among their aims, right?
But here's the problem: there is substantial evidence that many trans people face real-world violence, harassment, discrimination, and threats to their safety and health. Some are even driven into severe psychological distress, and in some cases toward suicide, by sustained hostility and abuse. So how can you draw such a clean line between “mere cultural or policy pushback” and the real-world harm produced by that hostility?
When that so-called “pushback” repeatedly translates into harassment, threats, discrimination, and real-world violence, at what point do you stop calling it “just cultural or policy pushback”?
